title: 2.2 Trends in Global Climate Change
description: Observed warming, greenhouse gas records, IPCC assessments and temperature projections. Medium level.

questions.question: Which century was likely the warmest in the last 1,000 years according to the 2001 report?
options: The twentieth century
The fifteenth century
The eighteenth century
The tenth century

questions.question: What did the IPCC project for global temperature by the end of the 21st century?
options: An increase of 20 degrees Celsius
It fixes the composition of rocks forever
An increase of 1.4 to 5.8 degrees Celsius
An increase of 0.1 degrees Celsius
questions.correctAnswer: An increase of 1.4 to 5.8 degrees Celsius

questions.question: What do ice cores help scientists reconstruct?
options: The depth of rivers
The migration of birds
Past atmospheric composition
A volcano on the ocean floor

questions.question: What did the 2001 assessment conclude about warming over the past 50 years?
options: It was caused by sunspots alone
All of it came from volcanic eruptions
Most of it resulted from human activities
An increase of 1.4 to 5.8 degrees Celsius
questions.correctAnswer: Most of it resulted from human activities

questions.question: How does the temperature record from 1880 onward support climate change?
options: Warming is small in any year and significant only over decades
A fracture forms and one limb is pushed forward over the other
Faster decomposition releases more carbon dioxide into the air
It shows a long-term rise in global land and ocean temperature
questions.correctAnswer: It shows a long-term rise in global land and ocean temperature

questions.question: What does in situ observation refer to?
options: Net greenhouse gas emissions offset by activities such as planting trees
It provides the reference against which temperature changes are measured
Direct measurements made at locations on the atmosphere, land and oceans
Subduction of one oceanic plate beneath another builds volcanic islands
questions.correctAnswer: Direct measurements made at locations on the atmosphere, land and oceans

questions.question: Why do scientists use multiple lines of evidence?
options: Changes in the shape of Earth orbit around the Sun
Together they confirm that the climate is changing
Climate is measured over years; weather over a day
Afforestation, reforestation and forest management
questions.correctAnswer: Together they confirm that the climate is changing

questions.question: What trend is expected for atmospheric composition in the 21st century?
options: It will become fixed forever
It will return exactly to preindustrial levels
It will contain no greenhouse gases
Human influence will continue to change it
questions.correctAnswer: Human influence will continue to change it

questions.question: Which greenhouse gas is measured in ice cores?
options: Methane
Oxygen
Nitrogen
Argon

questions.question: What role does the IPCC play in climate science?
options: It records the temperature of mountain peaks
It produces comprehensive assessment reports
The destruction of crust at subduction zones
Convergence, erosion, sedimentation, volcano
